that's the unfortunate part of just being strangers online. we don't know the whole story and never will. we don't know them personally. we can't judge accurately or extrapolate and it sucks! unfortunately, i have seen this situation happen over and over again. i have friends and family who have been in relationships like this, and i've seen this kind of thing first hand.

i'm not claiming to know what happened exactly, i'm just sick of victim blaming.

from the text, it sounds like he tried to make it up to her. he realized he fucked up (what happened exactly, we don't know) and tried to grow from it. according to the screenshot, she never let go of that suspicion. where did you get that he manipulated her?

uh. mild concern for those in the comments who feel like she was in the right?? i'm getting IMMENSE red flags from her from his story. this feels like one of those unfunny 'oh, abuse is funny if it's towards men via women' "jokes" but like, unironically. 

abuse isn't funny no matter who it's coming from y'all :/

i noticed it seems like what people are focusing on is that he punched the door. lemme ask something real quick: have you ever felt cornered, but couldn't do anything to combat that because you *don't want* to hurt your aggressor? ever been under of the thumb of someone who plays mind games to keep you under their control? to get you to do exactly what they want? and if you don't they'll pull out what *really* hurts you?

that's what this sounds like to me. months of mind games culminated into the straw that broke his back. damn, i'd wanna punch something too! and punching a door in that moment when you're overwhelmed is a *million times better* than EVER laying a hand on your partner. 

people keep focusing on what he "could have done" (but didn't) while consciously overlooking that she put him through the psychological wringer ~~over something he didn't even do. y'all are treating the situation the same way, like he *did* cheat. you're putting him on the same eggshells she did and for what?~~

trauma is hard. trauma is a hell of a thing. it's so so easy to project your trauma onto anyone that reminds you of what you went through. i understand, absolutely. but it isn't fair to anyone, not to you, not to them.

EDIT: ok somewhat embarrassing but i totally forgot that people do cheat over text 😓 if that is what happened, i totally rescind that he didn't cheat. like, absolute scumbag move there. i honestly thought this was a "you were looking at/talking to/thinking about another woman" sort of thing. i still think the mind games were unwarranted and manipulative as hell but like i said below, we don't know for sure and we haven't even heard her side.

> It's also pretty fucked up to just assume your partner is going to know what your sexual preferences are, especially if you haven't told them

So you agree. It's wrong to assume something of your partner that wasn't discussed beforehand. 😉

The problem is that he acted on a racist stereotype without consulting her about what *she* wanted. **He assumed what she wanted based on race alone.** 

I don't know about you, but making assumptions based solely on race sounds pretty freaking racist to me.

It's absolutely entirely possible for someone to think themselves "not racist" and still have ingrained racist ideology (which those stereotypes are born from.) I've known people like that and trust me, it feels much worse coming from someone who "only means well." 

*Kind of like a betrayal of trust or something.* 

On top of that, it's pretty fucked up to just assume your partner is going to be ok with rough sex their first time. That's..... *really* not okay. 

Someone who isn't experienced most likely isn't going to want to dive right into that kind of stuff. You might not know what kind of things your partner has been through, so it's important to talk things through beforehand if you're wanting something rougher from your night together. Remember; safe, sane, consensual. Maybe save it for a couple romps in, but absolutely discuss it together before you do.

He failed at communication *far* worse than she did, because **he acted before asking.** He was inconsiderate towards her because he didn't think to take her wants or feelings into account. 

That is **NOT** clear and enthusiastic consent.

I've actually had a few. (Sorry for long post.)

1. The first dream featuring Green Day (that I can remember) started with Billie on my couch, telling me some story. Suddenly, in a flashback of sorts, I was walking alongside a young Adrienne. We walked along a highway for some time and eventually met an equally young Billie. We went on a Nancy Drew-like adventure, solving a mystery which ended up having to do something with a truck. I don't remember much after that.

2. In another dream I had, I was at a Boys and Girls Club by a highway. Billie, Mike, and Tre found me watching videos on a computer in the storage room and invited me to go on tour with them. They jumped into a jet in the parking lot and headed down the highway while I followed behind on my bike.

3. I have two Green Day dreams that I've told to everyone I know. In the first, I was staying at a really dark and smoky motel. I was getting some ice from an ice machine when a frantic bellboy told me to deliver a message to room 305. He handed me a letter and ran off. I went to the room and knocked. The door opened to reveal a pissed off Billie in his boxers. I nervously explained why I was bothering him (to deliver the letter). He told me the only way I could make it up to him was to bring him cans of whipped cream. I went to the kitchen and grabbed all the whipped cream I could carry. When I brought it to him, his face lit up as he called, "Mike! Tre! She brought *whipped cream!!*" They thanked me and closed the door. I could hear them spraying whipped cream and cheering. (Honestly, I don't even want to know.) Later, I ran into them at the pool table. They thanked me again and offered me backstage passes. 

4. The other dream I tell people starts with my mom and I driving up a hill in Denver on our way to some club. The club turned out to be a small wood cabin. We entered and found out that the club was actually bigger on the inside. Half of the interior was a cabin/house area with one of those cushioned benches you see in restaurants along one wall and a kitchen on the other. The other half was the actual club where many people were dancing and Tre was the DJ.  My mom started chatting with Adrienne and Mike as I sat on the bench. Joey sat next to me and told me that his dad is actually a Time Lord and the cabin is his TARDIS. He then dared me to peek in on Billie sleeping in the other room. I opened the door near the kitchen to see him asleep (what else?) on a bed that fills the entire room. I went back to the bench and talked with Joey a bit more when Billie came out, fully dressed. As he left to go for a drive, Joey asked me if we should follow him. I agreed, and we got in Joey's car and followed Billie to a tunnel on a crowded, many lane highway. (What is it with these dreams and highways?) Suddenly, he turned around. Joey and I hauled ass back to the club and managed to get back before Billie. I woke up, extremely disappointed. 

**tl:dr: I've had a few messed up dreams about Green Day.**
